unlock.title: Unlock
unlock.label_hint: Distinguishes multiple passwords, e.g. Work, Personal
unlock.pick_folder_hint: Unlock parameters live in the files, so pick a folder before typing a password
unlock.quick_hint: Enter a password to unlock encrypted files in this folder
unlock.add_more_hint_one: 1 password loaded. Enter another to see more files; the current one stays.
unlock.add_more_hint_other: {{count}} passwords loaded. Enter another to see more files; the current ones stay.
unlock.already_loaded: That password is already in use; nothing was added

encrypt.filename_keep_ext_desc: Easier to identify, but reveals the file format
encrypt.compress_desc: Helps text and documents a lot, barely affects already-compressed media
encrypt.thumbnail_desc: Images and videos get a small preview stored alongside. It is encrypted too — only visible with the password.
encrypt.thumbnail_frame_hint: Leave empty to pick 10% in, skipping black intro frames. Accepts 83, 1:23 or 00:01:23.
encrypt.thumbnail_frame_bad: Can't read that timestamp. Use 83, 1:23 or 00:01:23.
encrypt.strength_sensitive_desc: 1 GiB · about 2 s, heavy on mobile
encrypt.original_trash_desc: Can still be restored from the system Recycle Bin
encrypt.original_delete_desc: Cannot be undone, and complete erasure is not guaranteed
encrypt.no_erase_note: This app does not offer "secure erase". SSD wear leveling makes overwrite-based erasure unreliable, and offering it would give a false sense of security.
encrypt.folder_note: Folder encryption is not implemented yet; selected folders will be skipped.
encrypt.folder_mode_container: Pack into a single encrypted file
encrypt.folder_mode_container_desc: Fully hides the directory structure; good for archiving and sharing. Changing any file rewrites the whole package.
encrypt.folder_mode_tree_desc: Supports incremental edits and cloud sync; individual files can be shared, and damage affects only one file.
encrypt.folder_mode_tree_leak: ⚠️ In per-file mode, others can see how many files you have, how large each one is, and how deep the directories go — but not the file names or contents.
encrypt.video_process_desc: Pick the cover frame while watching, and optionally convert before encrypting

video.title: Video processing
video.frame_hint: The scrubber, the timecode and the picture are three views of one value — change any of them and the others follow. Leave it empty to take the frame at one tenth of the duration, past the opening black frames.
video.none_desc: Encrypt as is; quality and size are untouched. Fastest and safest — nothing is re-encoded.
video.remux_desc: Changes only the container, never the video stream. As MP4 most files play directly, saving the on-the-fly remux at every playback.
video.compress_desc: Reduce resolution or bitrate to save space. Re-encodes, so it takes a while and costs some quality.
video.compress_blocked: Reduce resolution or bitrate to save space. Needs a video encoder, and this FFmpeg build has none.
video.compress_slow: Re-encoding is slow — a feature-length film can take tens of minutes. Please keep this window open.
video.faststart: faststart (move the index to the front)
video.faststart_desc: Without it, progressive playback must read to the end of the file before it can start
video.audio_drop_warn: ⚠️ This file's audio track is {{codec}}, which the target container cannot hold, and this FFmpeg has no AAC encoder — the result will have no sound. Switch to a full FFmpeg build, or choose MKV, to keep the audio.
video.sub_bitmap_warn: ⚠️ These are graphical subtitles (the Blu-ray / DVD kind — actually images). MP4 can neither hold them nor turn them into text, so they will disappear. Choosing MKV keeps them untouched.
video.sub_to_text_desc: Keeps the words, but loses fonts, colours, positioning and effects — mov_text is the only text subtitle MP4 accepts
video.sub_keep_style_desc: Requires the MKV container; slightly less compatible, but subtitles are untouched
video.sub_outcome_none: This file has no subtitle track.
video.sub_outcome_copy: Subtitles are kept as they are, styling included.
video.sub_outcome_to_mov_text: Subtitles become mov_text, MP4's standard text format; the content is unchanged.
video.sub_outcome_to_mov_text_lossy: Subtitles become mov_text — the words survive, the styling does not.
video.sub_outcome_drop: The result will carry no subtitles.
video.sub_outcome_bitmap_drop: Graphical subtitles cannot enter this container and will disappear.
video.sub_outcome_style_drop: With the current settings the subtitles will be dropped.
video.sub_style_needs_mkv: ⚠️ You chose to keep the styling, but the target is still MP4 — it cannot hold styled subtitles, so the result would have none at all.
video.caps_note: This FFmpeg build cannot compress video. The bundled one is trimmed to probing, frame extraction and remuxing, and carries no video encoder at all. Compression becomes available automatically with a full FFmpeg build — omy prefers the program named by OMY_FFMPEG, and you can also overwrite the files in the ffmpeg folder next to the application.
video.converted_no_audio: Note: the result has no audio track.
video.converted_no_subs: Note: the result has no subtitle track.
video.foot_frame_auto: Cover frame chosen automatically (one tenth in)

playback.cannot_preview: This format cannot be previewed in the app

view.empty_hint: Pick a place on the left to start browsing
view.start_hint: Browse files freely and encrypt what you select; double-click an encrypted file and enter its password to view it
view.name: Name

device.title: Devices & sharing
device.store_explain: The device store password protects this device's identity and its paired-device list. It is not the password for your encrypted files. Set one on first use.
device.fingerprint_hint: When pairing, check that both devices show the same fingerprints. A mismatch means someone is in the middle.
device.none_found: No devices found. Check that the other device is sharing and on the same network.
device.name_untrusted: Device names come from the other device's broadcast and cannot be trusted. Go by the fingerprint.
device.enter_pin: Pairing code shown on the other device
device.pin_hint: On the other device choose "Pair a device", enter this machine's address and port {{port}}, then type the code above. The code is valid for 2 minutes.
device.verify_hint: Confirm the other device shows these same two fingerprints.
device.share_no_password: Sharing does not need your file password: this device only sends ciphertext, and decryption happens on the other device. They still need the password to see anything.
device.share_no_peer: No devices paired yet, so nobody can connect.

remote.empty: This device is not sharing any files
remote.empty_hint: Ask them to pick a folder to share on their device.

errors.load_failed: Can't open this location. It may not exist or be readable.
errors.already_exists: A file or folder with that name already exists
errors.encrypted_dir_rename: Encrypted directories cannot be renamed; the name would become unrecoverable

recovery.restore_title: Reset password with a recovery code
recovery.generate_hint: A recovery code is 26 words. If you forget the password, it opens this file and lets you set a new one.
recovery.generate_why_password: You have to prove you can open this file today before adding another way in.
recovery.write_it_down: Write it on paper and keep it where you keep important documents. Do not photograph it, and do not put it in a notes app or a cloud-synced password manager entry.
recovery.warn_once: These words are shown once. We keep no plaintext copy, so once this window closes they are gone — you can only generate a new code, which voids this one.
recovery.warn_weakest: It opens the file just like a password does. Whoever holds that paper can open it, which makes it the floor on this file's security.
recovery.warn_no_scan: A file opened with a recovery code does not join directory scanning, so filenames in the list stay hidden. That is deliberate: a recovery code is an emergency way in, not a second everyday password.
recovery.warn_evicted: This claimed a new slot and may have overwritten another password that sat there. We cannot probe which slots are free — that is exactly what deniability requires — so all we can do is tell you honestly that it is possible.
recovery.acknowledge: I have written it down and understand it will not be shown again
recovery.restore_hint: Enter the 26 words you wrote down, then choose a new password.
recovery.code_hint: 26 words separated by spaces or newlines. Case and extra whitespace are ignored.
recovery.restore_note: The recovery code stays valid. You just had to use it, which means the password was already forgotten once — the worst possible moment to remove your only fallback.
recovery.generated_toast: Recovery code generated — write it down now
recovery.restored_toast: Password reset; the recovery code still works

keymgmt.title: Manage passwords
keymgmt.slots_hidden: How many passwords this file has cannot be determined: unused slots are filled with random data, indistinguishable from real ones. This is part of the deniability design.
keymgmt.add_desc: Both the current and the new password will open this file.
keymgmt.change_desc: The current password will no longer work afterwards.
keymgmt.remove_desc: Every other password on this file stops working (if there are any).
keymgmt.current_hint: Every operation above needs a password that can already open this file.
keymgmt.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match
keymgmt.same: The new password is the same as the current one
keymgmt.stale_copy_warning: Removing a password only affects this copy of the file. If it was copied, backed up or synced elsewhere, those copies can still be opened with the removed password. To make this file unrelated to the old password, choose "Re-encrypt" above.
keymgmt.payload_note: Only the header is rewritten; the content is not re-encrypted, so this is instant even for huge files.
keymgmt.done_add: Password added; both passwords now work
keymgmt.done_change: Password changed; the old one no longer works
keymgmt.done_remove: Only the current password is kept now
keymgmt.locked_hint: You need to be able to open this file before changing its passwords.
keymgmt.reencrypt_desc: Rewrites the whole file and replaces its file key. This file will no longer relate to the old password, but it takes time proportional to the file size.
keymgmt.reencrypt_warning: This file will be rewritten in full; large files may take a while, so please keep the app open. Afterwards the old password is useless for this file — but any copies made earlier are separate files and can still be opened with it.
keymgmt.next_optional_hint: Leave empty to keep the same password and only replace the file key — this makes the password on older copies useless for this file.
keymgmt.rewrite_note: The contents are re-encrypted, so this takes as long as the file is big. The original is left untouched until the write succeeds.
keymgmt.done_reencrypt: Re-encrypted; the file key has been replaced
keymgmt.tree_single_password: An encrypted folder shares one password across the whole tree, so it can only be changed, not added to or removed.
keymgmt.tree_warning: The folder's name is encrypted with the password too, so it will change to a different string once the password is changed (the contents are unaffected). The list will point at the new folder afterwards.
keymgmt.tree_reencrypt_warning: Every file in this tree will be rewritten; this takes time proportional to the total data size. Afterwards the old file keys are useless — but copies that already left your machine are separate ciphertext and still open with the password they had.

restore.target_pick_desc: Pick a location with the button below
restore.pick_title: Choose a folder to restore into
restore.pick_failed: Could not open the folder picker
restore.overwrite_desc: When off, existing files are skipped and reported
restore.container_note: A folder is restored as a directory of the same name, keeping its structure
restore.plaintext_note: Restored files are unencrypted — mind where you put them
restore.meta_not_recorded: modification time of single files (not saved at encryption)

ctx.single_only: Works on a single item only
ctx.key_needs_unlocked_file: Select a single unlocked encrypted file
ctx.recovery_needs_unlocked_file: Select a single unlocked encrypted file (folders not supported yet)
ctx.recovery_needs_file: Select a single encrypted file (folders not supported yet)
ctx.rename_encrypted_dir: This is an encrypted directory; its name is the ciphertext and renaming it would make the name unrecoverable
ctx.in_container_hint: Items inside a container have no file of their own on disk. Restore to disk first.
ctx.name_bad_trailing: Name cannot end with a dot or space

settings.title: Settings
settings.scan_scope_desc: Each remote file costs one request. Scanning all files is noticeably slower.
settings.concurrency_desc: Not a performance knob but a rate-limit boundary — raising it invites throttling.
settings.cache_ciphertext_note: The cache stores ciphertext only, identical to what is on the server; decrypted content is never written to disk.
settings.auto_lock_desc: Locking clears session keys; you will need the password again. Playback does not count as idle.
settings.lock_on_background_desc: A snapshot of the app enters the system task switcher, which others may see.
settings.wipe_temp: Delete as soon as the external app closes
settings.encrypt_defaults_note: These are only the initial values of the encrypt dialog; already-encrypted files are unaffected.
settings.original_action_desc: Kept by default. Deleting originals is irreversible and should not be the default.
settings.portable_desc: In portable mode, copying that folder takes all settings and cache with it.

rplace.title: Remote locations
rplace.name: Name
rplace.writable_desc: Leave unchecked to mount read-only, guarding against mistakes.
